posts.title: Claim 1 Year of Free Google AI (Gemini) for Students
posts.summary: A quick step-by-step guide for students to claim 1 year of free Google AI, verify with SheerID, and bypass portal errors.
posts.content:
# How to Claim 1 Year of Free Google Gemini for Students

Google is currently offering **one year of free access to Gemini Pro/Advanced** for university students. Follow the step-by-step guide below to claim your free subscription.

---

## Step-by-Step Application Guide

1. **Visit the Application Link**  
   Go to [gemini.google/students](https://gemini.google/students).

2. **Sign In with a Personal Google Account**  
   Log in using your personal `@gmail.com` address.  
   
> [!NOTE]
> Avoid using school-issued email domains if possible, as institutional security settings can sometimes block promotional sign-ups.

3. **Fill In Your Personal & University Details**  
   Enter your first name, last name, university name, and any other required student information.

4. **School Portal Redirect (If Applicable)**  
   The page may attempt to redirect you to a Microsoft or institutional login portal.  
   * **If the page fails to load or gives an error:** Close the tab, re-open the link, and restart the process.

5. **Verify Student Status via SheerID**  
   When prompted to provide proof of enrollment, take and upload a clear photo of your **Student ID card**. SheerID will review and verify your student status.

6. **Link Your Bank Card**  
   Add your debit/bank card to your Google Account to complete activation.  
   
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ensure you have at least **₦100** (or your local equivalent) in your bank account so Google can perform the initial authorization/card verification check.

7. **Complete Activation**  
   Once your card is linked and verified, confirm your claim to start your 1-year free subscription!

---

> [!WARNING]
> **Important Disclaimers**
> * **Claim Deadline:** Make sure to complete this process before the official promotional deadline set by Google.
> * **Auto-Renewal & Cancellation:** A payment card is required upfront to start the trial. If you do not wish to be billed when the free year ends, set a calendar reminder to **cancel the subscription before the 12-month period expires**.

posts.title: What building CodeOps Studio on a 2GB phone actually taught me
posts.summary: A longer look at the constraints, workarounds, and mindset shifts from building a full IDE without a laptop.
posts.content:
Every new coding session was a decision that required proper planning.

When your device can't brute-force its way through inefficiency, you're forced to actually understand what your tools are doing instead of throwing memory at the problem.

The OPPO A1K had **2GB of RAM** and coding on it was excruciatingly slow. Although coding on mobile device is feasible, I quickly hit a hardware and UX ceiling. I needed something that could handle:

- Real project structures
- Real linting
- Real CI hooks


So I built it.

## The hardest part

The hardest part wasn't the code. It was accepting that progress would be slow, and that **slow is not the same as worse**.

> Every crash taught me something a faster machine would have let me skip past.

I wouldn't recommend the constraint to anyone by choice, but I also wouldn't trade what it taught me.
